info.title: Edge CLI
info.description: The `edge-cli` command line and the `edge-engine` JSON REST API, generated from the route declarations in `src/cli/engine/routes/`.

tags.name: Lifecycle
tags.description: Lifecycle and configuration of the `edge-engine` daemon. None of these have an `edge-core-js` equivalent — they describe the daemon itself — and none need a session.

tags.name: Device and usernames
tags.description: Calls on the shared `EdgeContext`: local device state and login-server queries that do not need a session.

tags.name: Login methods
tags.description: Every successful login returns a [Session](#schema-Session) and registers it in the engine, so later calls need only the `sessionId`. The CLI writes that id to `session.json` automatically.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: Calls on a logged-in `EdgeAccount`, addressed by `sessionId`. All of these can also return `401 INVALID_SESSION` or `401 SESSION_EXPIRED`.

tags.name: Local settings
tags.description: Device-local account settings, stored outside the synced repos.

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description: Password, PIN, username and recovery changes on a logged-in account.

tags.name: Two-factor authentication
tags.description: OTP state and the reset flow a user falls back on after losing their authenticator.

tags.name: Vouchers
tags.description: When 2FA blocks a login, the login server issues a voucher an already-trusted device can approve or reject.

tags.name: Approving a login
tags.description: The other side of `request-edge-login`: a logged-in account inspecting and approving a login somebody scanned.

tags.name: Keys
tags.description: Raw key infrastructure beneath the wallet API. Several of these return private key material, and the engine has no transport auth — treat any process that can reach the socket as fully trusted.

tags.name: Wallet state
tags.description: Account-level wallet listing and creation, then per-wallet calls. A `{walletId}` segment accepts a unique prefix, so those routes can also return `404 WALLET_NOT_FOUND` or `409 AMBIGUOUS_WALLET_ID`.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: Which tokens a wallet tracks. Enabled tokens are the ones it syncs balances for; detected ones were seen on-chain but are not yet enabled.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description: Reading transaction history, exporting it, and editing its metadata.

tags.name: Object handles
tags.description: A core value with methods on it — a staged transaction, a swap quote, a pending login — cannot cross JSON, so the engine keeps it and hands back an id. These read and release any of them.

tags.name: Spending
tags.description: Two ways to send funds. `spend` does the whole thing in one call; the staged workflow — `make-spend`, `sign-tx`, `broadcast-tx`, `save-tx` — hands back an object handle at each step so fees can be inspected before committing.

tags.name: Swap quotes
tags.description: Cross-asset exchange. Quotes are live objects held server-side under a `swap_` handle, so approving one means naming its `objectId` rather than re-uploading the quote.

tags.name: URIs
tags.description: Parsing and building BIP21-style payment URIs through the wallet’s own plugin, so chain-specific quirks are handled for you.

tags.name: Exchange rates
tags.description: Historical and current rates through the same batching queue the GUI uses. No session required.

tags.name: Data store
tags.description: The account’s synced key-value store, where plugins keep their own state. One route per `EdgeDataStore` method.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: **Debugging only — not for production apps.** These reach into `context.$internalStuff`, the private surface of `edge-core-js`, and can corrupt an account’s synced repos. They take no `sessionId`: they act on the context, not on a logged-in account.

tags.name: Event stream
tags.description: A Server-Sent Events feed of engine activity, served outside the router because the response never ends.

post.description:
**Core call:** `context.requestEdgeLogin`

**Command line**

```
request-edge-login [--no-wait]
```

Asks the login server for a lobby another logged-in Edge device can approve. The returned `lobbyId` is what goes in the QR code.

extra.name: no-wait
extra.doc: Print the lobby and exit instead of polling, so the QR can be displayed while `poll-edge-login` watches the same handle from another process.

x-cli.notes: Prints the pending login, then polls every 2s for up to 5 minutes. On `done` it stores the session. With `--no-wait` it returns immediately and `poll-edge-login` takes over.

objectId.description: Handle for the value the engine is holding. Pass it to the calls that consume it.

pendingId.description: Same value as `objectId`, under the name the poll command takes.

kind.description: What the handle refers to, which decides the calls that accept it.

expiresAt.description: When the lobby closes and the QR code stops working.

uri.description: The `edge://` URI to render as a QR code for the phone to scan.

state.description: How far the login has got: `pending` before the phone scans, `started` once it has, and `done` when `session` is filled in.

username.description: Account that approved the login, known once the phone has scanned.

error.description: Why the login failed, set only when `state` is `error`.
